name: Dhu al-Hijjah
intro:
The month of Dhu al-Hijjah is full of events and memories. Lasting days, among the sweetest in the history of the Ahl al-Bayt (PBUT), are gathered in this month alongside heart-rending events.
The days 1, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 13, 14, 15, 18, 20, 22, 24, 25, 27, 29 and 30 carry these events, which we review.
Eid al-Ghadir, the birth of Imam Hadi (PBUH), Eid al-Adha, the outward caliphate of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), the Day of Mubahalah, the Day of Ring-Giving of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), and the revelation of Surah Hal Ata are days of joy for the Shia in this month. The martyrdom of Imam Baqir (PBUH), the taking of Imam Kazim (PBUH) to the prison of Basra, the martyrdom of Hazrat Muslim and Hani in Kufa, the martyrdom of Abd Allah al-Mahd and a group of the Al-Hasan (PBUT), the martyrdom of Maytham al-Tammar, and the death of Ali ibn Ja'far (PBUH) are counted among the days of sorrow of the Al-Muhammad (PBUT) in this month.
The death of Abu Bakr's father, the death of Hind the mother of Mu'awiyah, the killing of Umar, the killing of Uthman, the end of the thousand-month Umayyad dynasty, and the death of Mansur al-Dawaniqi are days that renew in the heart the disavowal (bara'ah) of the enemies of the Ahl al-Bayt (PBUT). The Day of Arafah, the splitting of the moon, the marriage of Amir al-Mu'minin and Hazrat Zahra (PBUT), the Battle of Sawiq, the Prophet's (SAWW) letters to the great kings, the Pledge of Aqabah, the gifting of Fadak to Hazrat Zahra (PBUH), the dismissal of Abu Bakr from conveying Surah Bara'ah, the Day of Closing the Doors to the Prophet's (SAWW) Mosque, the divulging of the secret of wilayah by Aisha, the plot to assassinate Imam Husayn (PBUH), Hazrat Muslim's (PBUH) public call in Kufa, Imam Husayn's (PBUH) departure from Mecca to Iraq, the day of writing Du'a al-Sabah, the first Friday prayer of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), the beginning of the letters for the Battle of Siffin, the Incident of Harrah, and the departure of Ibrahim ibn Malik al-Ashtar to fight Ibn Ziyad are each important and memorable chapters of Islamic history.

events.title: Dismissal of Abu Bakr from Conveying Surah Bara'ah
events.text:
On this day in the ninth year of the Hijrah, Abu Bakr was dismissed from conveying Surah Bara'ah. The Prophet (SAWW) then sent Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) to take the verses of Bara'ah from Abu Bakr and to recite them himself to the people of Mecca. The story began when, in the year 9 AH, the Prophet (SAWW) sent Abu Bakr to Mecca to recite the opening verses of Surah Bara'ah to the disbelievers. After he left, Gabriel descended: “O Messenger of God, this matter must be carried out either by you or by a man who is from you.” According to another narration: “Ali (PBUH) must convey it on your behalf.”
The Prophet (SAWW) appointed Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), who was in the position of his own soul, and said to him: Hurry, take the verses from Abu Bakr, and recite them to the people during the Hajj season.
The Dispatch of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) and the Return of Abu Bakr
The Prophet gave his she-camel Ghadba' to Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), and he set out together with Jabir ibn Abd Allah. On the second day he reached Abu Bakr, took the verses of Bara'ah from him, and left it to Abu Bakr himself to choose whether to come along or return. Abu Bakr returned to Medina and said to the Prophet (SAWW): “You deemed me fit for a task that others were eager for, yet after I had gone a short distance you dismissed me?” The Prophet said: “I did not dismiss you; rather, God dismissed you.”
The Conveying of Surah Bara'ah by Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH)
Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), during the three days of Tashriq in Mina, where the disbelievers and polytheists had gathered and were filled with hatred and enmity toward Ali (PBUH), recited the verses to the people every morning and evening, together with the sayings of the Prophet (SAWW), and then returned to Medina.
From the time Ali (PBUH) had gone to Mecca, signs of sorrow had appeared on the blessed face of the Prophet (SAWW) because of his absence. The companions said among themselves: Perhaps news of his death has come from heaven, or perhaps he has grown weary of us. Abu Dharr (may God have mercy on him) held a standing and rank with the Prophet (SAWW), so they sent him to the Prophet. Abu Dharr conveyed the companions' words, and the Prophet said: “My grief and sorrow is because of separation from Ali.” The Return of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) from Conveying Bara'ah
Abu Dharr set out from Medina to welcome Ali (PBUH) and learn of his condition, and on the way he met Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), greeted him, and said: May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, please come slowly so that I may go ahead and give the Prophet (SAWW) the glad tidings of your arrival.
Abu Dharr hurried to the Prophet (SAWW) and gave him the glad tidings of Ali's (PBUH) coming. The Prophet, together with his companions, came out to welcome Ali (PBUH), and when they reached him, he dismounted, embraced him, placed his blessed face on Ali's (PBUH) shoulder, and wept out of longing at seeing him, and Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) wept as well. Then the Prophet (SAWW) said to Ali (PBUH): “May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, what did you do in Mecca?” Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) informed him of all that had taken place.

events.title: Beginning of the Letters for the Battle of Siffin
events.text: Two days after the arrival of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) at Siffin, on the first of Dhu al-Hijjah, he wrote a letter to Mu'awiyah and admonished him, but in the end it was agreed that the war would begin on the first of Safar, after the sacred month, and on the first of Safar the war began. According to one account, his arrival was on 22 Muharram.
sources: Tatimmat al-Muntaha: p. 24.
Qala'id al-Nuhur: Muharram and Safar vol., p. 303.

events.title: Battle of Sawiq
events.text:
In this month in the year 2 AH, the Expedition of Sawiq took place. After the Battle of Badr, Abu Sufyan vowed not to approach a woman or anoint himself with oil until he took his revenge on the Prophet (SAWW). To this end, he went with two hundred men to Urayd, on the outskirts of Medina, and they set fire to two houses and several date palms and killed two prominent men of the Ansar there, so that he could claim to have fulfilled his vow.
When the news reached the Prophet (SAWW), he left Abu Lubabah in Medina and set out toward Urayd with two hundred of the Muhajirun and the Ansar, at their head Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH). When Abu Sufyan learned that the Prophet (SAWW) was coming there in haste, he ordered his army to pour out the sacks of sawiq (roasted barley flour) they had brought as provisions and to flee lightly laden. When the Muslims arrived, they had fled. So they took the sacks of sawiq and returned. For this reason, this expedition is called “Dhat al-Sawiq.”
sources: Bihar al-Anwar
Muntaha al-Amal: vol. 1, p. 58.

events.title: Marriage of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) and Hazrat Zahra (PBUH)
events.text: On this day in the year 2 AH, our master and lord, the Seal of the Prophets (SAWW), gave Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) in marriage to the Lady of the Women of the Worlds, Fatimah Zahra Batul 'Adhra' (PBUH). This event took place after returning from the Battle of Badr, 16 days after the death of Ruqayyah, the daughter of the Prophet (SAWW), on Tuesday, 6 Dhu al-Hijjah. Imam Sadiq (PBUH) said: “If God Almighty had not created Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), there would have been no one on the whole earth who was an equal and suitable spouse for Hazrat Fatimah (PBUH).”

subsections.title: The Proposal for Fatimah (PBUH)
subsections.text:
When the blessed age of Batul 'Adhra', Hazrat Siddiqah Tahirah Fatimah Zahra (PBUH), reached a full nine years, from every corner of Medina and from among the great tribes, the chiefs of the clans, and the possessors of wealth and means, people came to ask for her hand. A number of hypocrites also took the audacity to come proposing, with utter shamelessness. At the proposals of some of them, the Messenger of God (SAWW) was greatly distressed, and to a number of hypocrites who objected he said: “I have not rejected you; rather, God has rejected you, and the matter of Fatimah (PBUH) will be decided by God Almighty.” They were unaware that God had kept this precious jewel under the shelter of His honor and protection, and had not made her suited to the capacities of the sons of this world, whether kings or subjects, the poor or the rich; rather, He had reserved her for the successor of the Prophet (SAWW), Ali ibn Abi Talib, Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH).
It is narrated from Imam Husayn (PBUH) that he said: One day the Messenger of God (SAWW) was in the house of Umm Salamah. An angel of extraordinary majesty descended upon him, engaged in glorifying and sanctifying God in various languages unlike one another. He said: I am Sarsa'il. God has sent me to you to tell you: “Wed light to light.” The Prophet said: “Whom to whom?” He said: “Fatimah to Ali ibn Abi Talib.” So the Prophet (SAWW) concluded the marriage contract of Fatimah (PBUH) to Ali (PBUH) in the presence of Gabriel, Michael and Sarsa'il, and this contract took place on earth.
At this moment the Prophet (SAWW) looked between the shoulders of Sarsa'il and saw that it was written: There is no god but God, Muhammad is the Messenger of God, Ali ibn Abi Talib is the establisher of the proof. He said: O Sarsa'il, since when has this sentence been written between your shoulders? He said: Twelve thousand years before God Almighty created the world.

subsections.title: The Wedding Ceremony
subsections.text:
When Hazrat Fatimah (PBUH) was being taken to the house of Ali (PBUH) on the wedding night, the Prophet (SAWW) walked ahead of her, Gabriel at her right and Michael at her left, and seventy thousand angels behind her, glorifying and sanctifying God all the while, and this sanctification and glorification continued until the break of dawn.
Gabriel held the reins of the she-camel on which she was being carried, Israfil held the stirrup, and Michael followed behind it, and the Prophet (SAWW) was arranging the garments of Fatimah (PBUH), and seventy thousand angels together with other angels were proclaiming “Allahu Akbar.” But in outward appearance, Salman held the reins of the she-camel, and Hamzah, Aqil and Ja'far of the Ahl al-Bayt, and Banu Hashim with drawn swords, came behind Hazrat Fatimah (PBUH), while the wives of the Prophet (SAWW) came ahead.
The Prophet (SAWW) summoned them to the mosque, placed Fatimah's (PBUH) hand in Ali's (PBUH) hand, and said: Barak Allah fi ibnat Rasul Allah (“May God bless the daughter of the Messenger of God”); and he also said: Hadhihi wadi'ati (“This is my trust”); and after a special ceremony, the Prophet (SAWW) prayed for them and their descendants. Then he said: Marhaban bi-bahrayn yaltaqiyan wa najmayn yaqtarinan (“Welcome to two seas that meet and two stars that unite”).
Then the Prophet (SAWW) came out from beside them, took hold of the doorframe, and said: Tahharakuma Allah wa tahhara nasl-akuma, ana silm li-man salamakuma wa harb li-man harabakuma, astawdi'ukuma Allah wa astakhlifuhu 'alaykuma (“May God purify you both and purify your offspring; I am at peace with whoever is at peace with you and at war with whoever wars against you; I entrust you both to God and appoint Him as guardian over you”).
Then everyone went to their homes, and of the women no one remained with Fatimah (PBUH) except Asma', and this was because of the testament of Hazrat Khadijah (PBUH), who wept at the time of her death and took a pledge from Asma' not to leave Hazrat Fatimah (PBUH) alone on her wedding night. Asma' kept her promise, and when she related the matter to the Prophet (SAWW), he remembered Khadijah (PBUH), wept, and prayed for Asma'.
sources: Iqbal al-A'mal: p. 584. Tarikh Baghdad: vol. 5, p. 7.

subsections.title: The Dowry of Hazrat Zahra (PBUH)
subsections.text:
Various narrations have been reported regarding the amount and kind of her dowry:
A long black garment, a sheepskin, and some perfume.
A soft, gentle garment and a Khatti coat of mail made in Bahrain.
Four hundred and eighty dirhams.
Four hundred mithqals of silver.
Five hundred dirhams, about which Allamah Majlisi (may God have mercy on him) says: this is the most authentic of the accounts.
A Hutami coat of mail worth thirty dirhams, and the skin of a ram or ewe.
A Hutami coat of mail.
A camel.
One fifth of the earth. The Prophet (SAWW) said: “It has been decreed in heaven that the dowry of Zahra is one fifth of the earth. So whoever walks on the earth while being an enemy of her and her children, his walking on it is forbidden until the Day of Resurrection.”
Imam Baqir (PBUH) said: The dowry of Fatimah (PBUH) is one fifth of the world and two thirds of Paradise, and of the rivers on earth, the four rivers the Euphrates, the Nile, the Nahrawan and Balkh belong to Hazrat Fatimah (PBUH). God said to the Prophet (SAWW): “O Muhammad, marry Fatimah to Ali for a dowry of five hundred dirhams, so that it may be a tradition among your community.” In another narration: “One quarter of the world, and Paradise and Hell, so that she admits her friends into Paradise and sends her enemies to Hell.” In another narration, her dowry is mentioned as half of the world.

subsections.title: The Wedding Banquet
subsections.text: The household furnishings and the wedding banquet of Hazrat Zahra (PBUH) were as follows: the Prophet (SAWW) said to Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH): “Sell your coat of mail.” He sold the coat of mail and brought the money to the Prophet (SAWW). The Prophet (SAWW) gave a portion of it to Umm Salamah for preparing the wedding meal. According to some narrations, half of the provisions for the meal were prepared by the Prophet (SAWW) and the other half by Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH).

subsections.title: The Trousseau of Hazrat Zahra (PBUH)
subsections.text:
A portion was also given to Bilal and Ammar to buy household necessities from the market: a shirt, a headscarf, a black Khaybari blanket or a black cloak, a thin woolen curtain, a mat woven in the village of Hajar, a hand mill, a copper basin, a waterskin for carrying water, an earthenware bowl, a special waterskin for cooling water, a pitcher whose outer side was colored, an earthenware jug, and a sheepskin.
Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) says: On that night when the daughter of the Prophet (SAWW) came to my house, our bed was nothing but a sheepskin.
In another place it is narrated from him that he said: I married Fatimah (PBUH) at a time when we had nothing but a sheepskin on which we slept at night and on which we poured our camel's fodder by day, and we had no servant in the house.
In another narration he says: The Prophet (SAWW) came to our house while we had thrown a blanket over ourselves such that if we pulled it lengthwise over ourselves our sides were left uncovered, and if we spread it widthwise our heads and feet were left uncovered.
Some of the Sunnis have reported: When Fatimah (PBUH) went to the house of Ali (PBUH), she found nothing in his house but spread-out pebbles, an earthenware jug, a pillow, and a vessel for water.
According to another account, two small jugs, a milk vessel carved from wood, a green-colored jar into which oil or flour was poured, and four pillows or cushions or bolsters covered with skin and filled with dried green plants were among the household items.

subsections.title: The Wedding and Its Participants
subsections.text:
In some narrations it is reported that after the purchase, Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) waited 29 or thirty days until Ja'far and Aqil said to him: We ask the Prophet (SAWW) to have you bring your wife.
The Prophet (SAWW) said: “We are waiting for him to come himself and ask us.” Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) says: I said: “Modesty prevents me.” The Prophet (SAWW) permitted the wedding gathering and banquet, and said to Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH): “Invite whomever you wish.” The women saw to the affairs of the women, while Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), Ammar, Bilal and a few others saw to the men's gathering, which was in the mosque.
The companions took part with their gifts in the wedding celebration of those two divine lights, and ate from the wedding banquet that had been prepared at the command of the Prophet (SAWW). At that gathering 4,000 people ate of that food, and the Prophet (SAWW) sent food for Amir al-Mu'minin and Fatimah (PBUT), and nothing of that food diminished; it remained as it was, even though they ate of it for three days.
That night, with a special ceremony, by order of the Prophet (SAWW), the two honored ones were brought to the chamber of Umm Salamah.
Umm Salamah says: When the sun set, the Prophet (SAWW) said: “Bring Fatimah.” I went and took Fatimah's (PBUH) hand, her garment trailing on the ground and sweat flowing from her face out of modesty and shyness, and brought her to her honored father. When she reached him, her foot slipped from extreme shyness. The Prophet (SAWW) said: “May God keep you from slips in this world and the next.”
When she stood before him, he drew the veil back from Fatimah's (PBUH) face so that Ali (PBUH) could see her face. Then he placed her hand in Ali's (PBUH) hand, and thus that luminous life began.
sources: Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 43, p. 96.

subsections.title: The Fruit of the Luminous Marriage
subsections.text:
The fruit of this blessed, luminous and divine marriage was five children. Two infallible Imams, our master and lord Hazrat Mujtaba (PBUH) and the Master of the Martyrs Hazrat Aba Abd Allah (PBUH), and two daughters, Hazrat 'Aqilat Bani Hashim Zaynab al-Kubra and Lady Umm Kulthum (PBUT); these children were born during the lifetime of the Prophet (SAWW), within a period of nine years. Their last child was Hazrat Muhsin (PBUH), who, some days after the martyrdom of the Prophet (SAWW), was martyred by blows between the door and the wall and the beatings of the hypocrites and oppressors.
Hazrat Fatimah (PBUH) lived in the house of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) for nine years and 75 or 95 days, until she was martyred after the martyrdom of Hazrat Muhsin (PBUH).
sources: Dala'il al-Imamah of Tabari: pp. 45, 47.

subsections.title: The Heavenly Marriage
subsections.text: Between the marriage of those honored ones in heaven and their wedding on earth there was an interval of forty days. On the first or sixth of Dhu al-Hijjah, with God Almighty as the party offering the contract and Gabriel as the party accepting, and Rahil as the one reciting the sermon, the witnesses were the bearers of the Throne and 70 thousand angels. The one who scattered gifts at this wedding was Ridwan, the keeper of Paradise's treasury, and what was scattered was pearls, rubies and coral, and the attendant of the bridal chamber of this union was Asma'.
sources: Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 43, p. 97.

events.title: Death of Mansur al-Dawaniqi
events.text: On this day in the year 158 AH, Mansur al-Dawaniqi, the miserly and merciless, perished on a Hajj journey and was buried at Hajun. Among the Abbasids, Mansur bore a complete resemblance to Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik among the Umayyads, and imitated him. He was a bloodthirsty man, and unlike his brother Saffah, he bore complete enmity and oppression toward the descendants of Abu Talib. He killed many of those honored ones, and Mansur's greatest crime was the martyrdom of Imam Sadiq (PBUH). He also martyred Abd Allah al-Mahd, Hasan al-Muthallath and many of Banu al-Hasan.
sources: Tatimmat al-Muntaha: p. 160. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 109. Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 5, p. 220.

events.title: Martyrdom of Imam Baqir (PBUH)
events.text:
On such a day, a Monday, in the year 114 AH, Imam Baqir (PBUH) was poisoned and martyred by Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik. On the night of his martyrdom he said to Imam Sadiq (PBUH): “Tonight I shall bid farewell to the world. Just now I saw my father Ali ibn al-Husayn bring me a delightful drink, and I drank it, and he gave me glad tidings of the eternal abode and of meeting the Truth.” In another narration he said: O dear son, have you not heard Hazrat Ali ibn al-Husayn call me from behind the wall: “O Muhammad, come, hurry, for we are awaiting you.”
For several days, or according to one account three days, he remained in pain from the effect of the poison until he was martyred. The next day, the pure and purified body of that boundless ocean of divine knowledge was laid to rest in the earth of Baqi', beside the graves of Imam Mujtaba and Imam Sajjad (PBUT).
He bequeathed eight hundred dirhams for his mourning and lamentation. Hazrat Sadiq (PBUH) said: My father said: “O Ja'far, set aside a portion of my property as an endowment for lamenters who will weep for me for ten years in Mina during the Hajj season and renew the mourning ceremonies.”
Our master and lord Hazrat Baqir (PBUH) had the honor of being present at Karbala. On the eleventh night, he saw the Kufa marketplace beside the pure heads, the captivity in Sham and the assembly of Yazid, and whenever he recalled the martyrdom of Husayn ibn Ali (PBUH) and the captivity of his aunts, tears flowed from his blessed eyes like pearls.
sources: Tawdih al-Maqasid: p. 29. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 110.

events.title: Imam Kazim (PBUH) Taken to the Prison of Basra
events.text:
On this day Imam Kazim (PBUH) was taken to Basra in shackles and chains and was imprisoned for one year with Isa ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Ja'far Mansur, and then the Imam was taken to Baghdad. Isa imprisoned him in one of the rooms of his house that was close to the administrative office, and busied himself with merrymaking. It is narrated from one of his scribes, a Christian, that he said: “This righteous servant and fitting slave of God, that is Musa ibn Ja'far (PBUH), during the days he was imprisoned in this house, heard things of amusement and frivolity that I do not think had ever crossed his noble mind.”
Our master and lord Hazrat Kazim (PBUH) was imprisoned in Basra for one year, and after one year the Imam was taken to Baghdad and imprisoned with Fadl ibn Rabi'.
sources: Fayd al-'Allam: p. 111.

events.title: Plot to Assassinate Imam Husayn (PBUH)
events.text: On this day in the year 60 AH, by order of the accursed Yazid, thirty of the devils of Banu Umayyah entered Mecca from Sham, under the pretext of Hajj, to arrest or kill Imam Husayn (PBUH).
sources: Qala'id al-Nuhur: Dhu al-Hijjah vol., p. 375. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 113.

events.title: Hazrat Muslim's (PBUH) Public Call in Kufa
events.text: On this day in the year 60 AH, a Tuesday, Hazrat Muslim (PBUH) made public his call for Imam Husayn (PBUH) in Kufa, and on the other side the people of Kufa revealed their hypocrisy.
sources: Irshad: vol. 2, p. 66. I'lam al-Wara: vol. 1, p. 445. Masar al-Shi'ah: p. 17. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 112. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 44, p. 363.

events.title: Imam Husayn's (PBUH) Departure from Mecca to Iraq
events.text: On this day in the year 60 AH, Imam Husayn (PBUH) set out from Mecca toward Iraq, and this is the well-known view among the hadith scholars and the authors of maqatil. According to one account, he set out from Mecca toward Iraq on the ninth.
sources: Irshad: vol. 2, p. 66. I'lam al-Wara: vol. 1, p. 445. Masar al-Shi'ah: p. 17. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 44, p. 363.
Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 44, p. 366.

events.title: Day of Arafah
events.text: On the Day of Arafah, visiting Imam Husayn (PBUH) is recommended, for God first looks upon the visitors of Imam Husayn (PBUH), because all of them are of lawful birth, and then looks upon His knowledgeable visitors at Arafat.
sources: Masar al-Shi'ah: p. 18. Tawdih al-Maqasid: p. 30. Misbah al-Kaf'ami: vol. 2, p. 600.
Zad al-Ma'ad: p. 262. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 97, p. 384.

events.title: Martyrdom of Hazrat Muslim and Hani
events.text: On this day in the year 60 AH, Muhammad ibn Kathir and his son were martyred in Kufa on the charge of hosting and supporting Muslim ibn Aqil (PBUH). On the eve of Arafah, Muslim ibn Aqil (PBUH) went to the house of Taw'ah. On the Day of Arafah of the year 60 AH, which was a Wednesday, Muslim ibn Aqil and Hani ibn Urwah were martyred in Kufa.
sources: Fayd al-'Allam: p. 113.
Irshad: vol. 2, p. 66. I'lam al-Wara: vol. 1, p. 445. Misbah al-Kaf'ami: vol. 2, p. 600. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 44, p. 363. Masar al-Shi'ah: p. 18. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 115.

subsections.title: The Family of Hazrat Muslim
subsections.text:
His blessed name was Muslim, his father was Aqil, his mother was 'Aliyyah, and his wife was Ruqayyah, the daughter of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH).
The Prophet (SAWW) said: “The eyes of the believers weep for him, and the angels near to God send blessings upon him.” When Imam Husayn (PBUH) sent him to Kufa, in part of the letter to the people of Kufa he said: “I have sent to you my brother, my cousin, and the one I trust from among my household.” When Imam Husayn (PBUH) heard the news of his martyrdom and that of Hani, he said several times: “Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un.” Then he said: “There is no good in life after them.” Among his bequests to Ibn Sa'd was that someone be sent to Imam Husayn (PBUH) so that the Imam would not come toward Kufa.
sources: Muruj al-Dhahab: vol. 3, pp. 69, 70. Maraqid al-Ma'arif: vol. 2, pp. 307, 316. Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: pp. 292, 293. Fursan al-Hayja': vol. 1, pp. 62, 120.

subsections.title: The Martyrdom and Burial of the Body of Hazrat Muslim
subsections.text:
Of his strangeness and oppression it suffices to say that from the rooftops they set bundles of reeds on fire and poured them upon him. Also, when Ibn Ziyad's eyes fell on him, he opened his tongue in insolence toward Amir al-Mu'minin, Imam Husayn (PBUT) and Aqil. On top of Dar al-Imarah, with parched lips, they severed his head from his dear body and threw his body down from the top of the palace. After his martyrdom they tied a rope to his blessed feet and dragged him through the Kufa marketplace. Then they hanged his blessed body and sent his pure head to Damascus.
There are two views regarding the burial of his pure body: one is that a group from the tribe of Hani came and buried the pure bodies of Muslim ibn Aqil and Hani. The other is that in the middle of the night the wife of Maytham al-Tammar, together with several people including the wife of Hani ibn Urwah, buried the bodies beside the Great Mosque of Kufa.
sources: Maraqid al-Ma'arif: vol. 2, p. 318. Fursan al-Hayja': vol. 2, p. 106.
Wasilat al-Darayn: p. 209, from al-Tha'labi.

subsections.title: Hani ibn Urwah
subsections.text:
As for Hani, whose father was Urwah, he was a companion of the Prophet (SAWW), one of the elders and elite of the Shia, and among the sincere in love of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), and he served him in the battles of Siffin, Jamal and Nahrawan.
Hani was the chief of the tribe of Madhhij and held great influence within his tribe. When the people of Kufa broke their covenant and proved their faithlessness toward the Ahl al-Bayt (PBUT) and Muslim ibn Aqil (PBUH), Hani ibn Urwah gave him refuge. After that, the vile Muhammad ibn al-Ash'ath arrested Hani and a number of Shia.
After the martyrdom of Muslim ibn Aqil, and after Hani's head and nose were broken by the accursed Ibn Ziyad, that vile man ordered that Hani's head be severed from his body in the sheep-sellers' market, and with a rope tied to his feet he was dragged along the ground, together with the body of Muslim ibn Aqil (PBUH), through the Kufa marketplace, and then they hanged him; and then Hani's body was buried together with the body of Muslim.
sources: Maraqid al-Ma'arif: vol. 2, pp. 318, 359, 361. Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: pp. 294, 295. Fursan al-Hayja': vol. 2, pp. 139, 143. Wasilat al-Darayn: pp. 208, 209.

events.title: Day of Closing the Doors
events.text:
On this day, by order of the Prophet (SAWW), all the doors of the companions' houses opening toward the Prophet's (SAWW) mosque were closed, except the door of the house of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), which by a special divine command was not closed. A number of companions said: O Messenger of God, why did you close all the doors except the door of Ali's (PBUH) house? The Prophet said: “I follow the revelation of my Lord,” and in another narration the Prophet (SAWW) delivered a sermon in which he said: “O people, God Almighty commanded Moses and Aaron to build houses, and commanded that those in a state of major ritual impurity not spend the night in those houses and that women not enter them, except Aaron and the descendants of Aaron. Ali ibn Abi Talib (PBUH) is to me as Aaron was to Moses. So it is not permissible for any woman or anyone in a state of major ritual impurity to enter my mosque.”
The Prophet (SAWW) stood and said: “Some are not content at heart that Ali ibn Abi Talib (PBUH) should dwell in the mosque at all times and in every state while they have been put out. By God, I did not put them out, and I did not make Ali (PBUH) dwell in the mosque; rather, God put them out and made Ali (PBUH) dwell in the mosque, and his standing with me is like the standing of Aaron with Moses (PBUH).” Then he spoke words on the virtues of Ali (PBUH), until he said: “Whoever is upset by this, let him go there,” and he pointed toward Sham.
sources: Tawdih al-Maqasid: p. 30. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 97, p. 384; vol. 95, p. 189. Misbah al-Kaf'ami: vol. 2, p. 600. Waqa'i al-Shuhur: p. 226.
'Ilal al-Shara'i': vol. 1, p. 262. Tadhkirat al-Khawass of Ibn al-Jawzi: p. 46.

events.title: Eid al-Adha
events.text: It is the day of Eid al-Adha, and on this day the pilgrims of the Sacred House of God are in Mina for stoning the Jamarat and offering sacrifice.
sources: Tawdih al-Maqasid: p. 30. Masar al-Shi'ah: p. 18.

events.title: Martyrdom of Abd Allah al-Mahd and a Group of the Al-Hasan (PBUT)
events.text:
On this day in the year 145 AH, Abd Allah al-Mahd ibn Hasan al-Muthanna ibn Imam Hasan Mujtaba (PBUH), at the age of 57, together with a group of his brothers and cousins, was martyred in the prison of Mansur al-Dawaniqi (may God's curse be upon him). Their prison was such that day and night could not be distinguished in it.
The brothers of Abd Allah al-Mahd were Hasan and Ibrahim, and the mother of these two honored ones was Fatimah bint al-Husayn (PBUH). The sons of the uncle of Abd Allah al-Mahd were Ya'qub, Ishaq, Abu al-Hasan Ali al-'Abid, Abbas and Abd Allah. Some of these honored ones, such as Ibrahim ibn Hasan, were buried alive. Others were martyred when the ceiling was brought down upon them while they were inside a house. The resting place of the Al-Hasan (PBUH) is in Hashimiyyah near Baghdad, which is known as the Seven Graves.
Because of the particular enmity he held toward the Ahl al-Bayt (PBUT), some time before the martyrdom of those honored ones, in the year 144 AH, Mansur ordered that the Al-Hasan (PBUT) be mounted, with shackles and chains on their necks and feet, on unruly mounts without any saddle cloth, and taken to Rabadhah. In that state they were held, with bare bodies, before the sun in front of Mansur. Abd Allah al-Mahd addressed Mansur, saying: “Did we do this to your captives on the day of Badr?” These words were heavy on Mansur, and he rose and left.
When those honored ones were being taken out of Medina in that state, Imam Sadiq (PBUH) looked at them from behind a curtain and wept so much that tears flowed down his blessed beard and said: By God, after this group they have not preserved any sanctity for God.
sources: Maraqid al-Ma'arif: vol. 2, p. 15. Kitab al-Mu'aqqibin min Walad al-Imam Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH): pp. 123, 124.
Maraqid al-Ma'arif: vol. 2, p. 19. Maqatil al-Talibiyyin: pp. 144, 196, 205.

events.title: Imam Reza's (PBUH) Eid Prayer in Khorasan
events.text: On this day our master and lord, Hazrat Thamin al-Hujaj (PBUH), at the request of Ma'mun, came out in Khorasan for the Eid prayer. Ma'mun, seeing the crowd of people gathering to take part in the prayer led by the Imam, ordered him to turn back midway, because he feared the people would rise against him. It was on the return from this prayer that Hazrat Reza (PBUH) asked God for death.
sources: Qala'id al-Nuhur: Dhu al-Hijjah vol., p. 383.

events.title: Day of Writing Du'a al-Sabah
events.text: On this day Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), taught by the Prophet (SAWW), wrote the noble Du'a al-Sabah with his own blessed hand.
sources: Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 91, p. 247.

events.title: Divulging of the Secret of Wilayah by Aisha
events.text:
On this day in the tenth year of the Hijrah, during the Farewell Pilgrimage, the Prophet (SAWW) confided a secret to Hafsah and warned her that if she told this secret to anyone, the curse of God, the angels and all people would be upon her.
Hafsah immediately told that secret to Aisha. Aisha in turn told it to Abu Bakr, and Abu Bakr informed Umar. The matter reached the point where those four, women and men, decided to poison the Prophet (SAWW).
Gabriel informed the Prophet (SAWW), and he told them about the plot and the divulging of the secret. Then he divorced Hafsah, but later, at the insistence of some, he took her back, and the verses of Surah al-Tahrim were revealed.
What had these two women done that God, in Surah al-Tahrim, likened them to the wives of Noah and Lot (PBUT)?! At the end of verse 4 of this surah it is said: if you two women support one another to kill him, God, Gabriel and the righteous of the believers, that is Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), and the angels are supporters of the Prophet (SAWW); the word “tazahara” in the noble verse is addressed to Aisha and Hafsah, and its meaning is that they cooperated in harming the Prophet (SAWW), divulged his secret, and harmed his wives. Umar says: the two women who were allies in harming the Prophet (SAWW) are Aisha and Hafsah.
sources: Waqa'i al-Shuhur: p. 229. Tafsir al-Qurtubi: vol. 5, p. 172.

و اذا أسر النبی الی بعض ازواجه حدیثا فلما نباءت به و أظهره الله علیه عرف بعضه و أعرض عن بعض فلما نباها به قالت من أنباک هذا قال نبانی العلیم الخبیر. ان تتوبا الی الله فقد صغت قلوبکما و ان تظاهرا علیه فان الله هو مولاه و جبریل و صالح المؤمنین و الملائکه بعد ذلک ظهیر (Surah al-Tahrim: verses 3 and 4).

ضرب الله مثلا للذین کفروا امره نوح و امراه لوط کانتا تحت عبدین من عبادنا صالحین فخانتهما فلم یغنیا عنهما من الله شیئا و قیل ادخلا النار مع الداخلین (Surah al-Tahrim: verse 10). Riyahin al-Shari'ah: vol. 2, pp. 382, 383. Quoted from the tafsirs of Khazin al-Baghdadi, Fakhr al-Razi and al-Zamakhshari. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 22, p. 233.
Tafsir al-Burhan: vol. 4, pp. 352, 353. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 22, pp. 228, 231.
Riyahin al-Shari'ah: vol. 2, pp. 382, 383. Quoted from the tafsirs of Khazin al-Baghdadi, Fakhr al-Razi and al-Zamakhshari.
Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 22, p. 232. Sahih al-Bukhari: vol. 6, pp. 195, 197.

events.title: Splitting of the Moon
events.text:
On the night of 14 Dhu al-Hijjah, the event of the splitting of the moon took place in Mecca by the miracle of the Prophet (SAWW). Some have placed this event on the night of the 18th of this month.
The Quraysh demanded a miracle from him, and the Prophet pointed with his finger at the moon, and by divine power it split in two and then joined together again; and the verse was revealed: Iqtarabat al-sa'ah wa inshaqqa al-qamar (“The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split”). Abu Jahl said: “This is sorcery! Send word and ask the other cities too whether they saw the moon split in two.” When the people of other cities were asked, they too reported that half of the moon fell behind the Kaaba and half onto Mount Abu Qubays.
sources: Riyahin al-Shari'ah: vol. 2, p. 257. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 120. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 17, pp. 350, 353.
Surah al-Qamar: verse 1.
Haqq al-Yaqin: p. 28. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 17, pp. 350, 353.

events.title: The Gifting of Fadak to Hazrat Zahra (PBUH)
events.text: On this day or the night of it, in the seventh year of the Hijrah, Fadak was gifted to Hazrat Zahra (PBUH), and the Messenger of God (SAWW) took witnesses to this gift. Another account on this matter is 15 Rajab.
sources: Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 95, p. 189. Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 2, p. 216.
Misbah al-Kaf'ami: vol. 2, p. 598.

subsections.title: The Conquest of Fadak
subsections.text:
After the conquest of Khaybar in the seventh year of the Hijrah, about four years before the martyrdom of the Prophet (SAWW), Gabriel descended and brought the command for the conquest of Fadak by the Prophet and Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUT). Those two honored ones came to the land of Fadak in the darkness of night with the necessary weapons, and by order of the Prophet (SAWW), Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) stood upon the shoulder of the Prophet (SAWW), and the Prophet rose and lifted Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) with him. By a divine miracle, the Master of the Monotheists (PBUH), with the sword of the Messenger of God (SAWW) with him, climbed the wall of the Fadak fortress and, atop the wall, raised his blessed voice in the call to prayer.
The Jews of the Fadak fortress thought that the Muslims had attacked and were on the walls. They wanted to flee through the fortress gate, but outside the fortress, in front of the gate, they saw the Prophet (SAWW) before them, and on the other side Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) came down and fought them, and they killed 18 of their leaders, and the rest surrendered.
They took their women and children captive and brought the spoils with them. It was decided that whoever of the people of Fadak became Muslim, a fifth of his property would be taken, and whoever remained in his religion, all his property would be taken. Thus, without any military campaign and without the slightest intervention of the Muslims, the Fadak fortress was conquered. And according to the blessed verse of Surah al-Hashr, lands conquered without a military campaign by the Muslims, even if their people come to the Prophet (SAWW) of their own accord in submission, these regions, their spoils and their captives belong exclusively to the Prophet, and like his personal property he may decide whatever he wishes concerning them, and the Muslims have no right in them.
sources: Surah al-Hashr: verses 6, 7.

subsections.title: The Granting of Fadak to Fatimah (PBUH)
subsections.text:
After this event Gabriel descended and brought this verse: Wa ati dha al-qurba haqqahu: “Give the relatives their due.”
The Prophet (SAWW) asked: Who is meant, and which right is this? Gabriel said from God: Grant Fadak to Fatimah (PBUH). The Prophet (SAWW) said to Hazrat Zahra (PBUH): “God conquered Fadak for your father, and since the army of Islam did not conquer it, it is exclusively mine. God has commanded that I give it to you. On the other hand, the dowry of your mother Hazrat Khadijah (PBUH) remains owed by your father, and in return for your mother's dowry, and by God's command, your father grants Fadak to you. Take it for yourself and your children, and be its owner.”
Hazrat Zahra (PBUH) said: “As long as you are alive, you have authority over me and my property.” The Prophet (SAWW) said: I fear that the unworthy will make your not taking possession during my lifetime a pretext and prevent you from it after me. Hazrat Siddiqah (PBUH) said: Act as you see fit. The Prophet (SAWW) summoned Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) and said: “Write and record the deed of Fadak as the Prophet's gift and grant.” Ali (PBUH) wrote it, and the Prophet (SAWW) and Umm Ayman bore witness, and the Prophet (SAWW) said: Umm Ayman is a woman of Paradise.
sources: Surah al-Isra': verse 26.

subsections.title: The Income of Fadak
subsections.text:
The Messenger of God (SAWW) gathered the people in the house of Hazrat Zahra (PBUH) and informed them that Fadak belonged to Fatimah (PBUH), and he distributed among the people the income of Fadak as a grant of Fatimah (PBUH).
The income of Fadak has been recorded at from seventy thousand to one hundred and twenty thousand gold coins annually. Every year the eyes of many of the needy were waiting for the arrival of the income of Fadak.

subsections.title: The Usurpation of Fadak
subsections.text:
After the passing of the Prophet (SAWW), Abu Bakr's agents, on his orders, expelled the representative of Hazrat Siddiqah (PBUH) from Fadak, usurped its ownership, and spent its income entirely on the expenses of their usurping government.
Hazrat Siddiqah (PBUH) brought to Abu Bakr that very writing and deed of Fadak that the Prophet (SAWW) had told Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) to write and that he had recorded, but Abu Bakr accepted neither the deed nor the witnesses.
Fifteen days after the martyrdom of the Prophet (SAWW), Hazrat Siddiqah the Martyr (PBUH), together with a group of the women of Banu Hashim, went to the mosque and delivered a sermon containing an ocean of knowledge, truths of eloquence and rhetoric, and the laws of Islam.
Abu Bakr wrote a letter to return it to her, but as Fatimah Zahra (PBUH), holding that deed, was returning home, she encountered Umar, who took Abu Bakr's writing from her with insolence toward her heavenly sanctity.
sources: Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 21, pp. 22, 25; vol. 29, p. 123.

events.title: Birth of Imam Hadi (PBUH)
events.text:
Imam Hadi (PBUH), according to the well-known account, was born on such a day in the year 212 or 214 AH, in the village of Surya near Medina. His birth has also been reported on 27 Jumada al-Thani and on 2, 3, 5 and 13 Rajab. His blessed name was “Ali,” the name of his father was Jawad al-A'immah (PBUH), and the name of his mother was Samanah al-Maghribiyyah, known as Sayyidah, with the kunyah Umm al-Fadl.
His noble kunyah is Abu al-Hasan the Third.
The titles of the Imam were: Najib, Murtada, Hadi, Naqi, 'Alim, Faqih, Amin, Mu'taman, al-Tayyib, 'Askari, Faqih 'Askari, and Ibn al-Rida.
sources: Tawdih al-Maqasid: p. 30. al-Kafi: vol. 2, p. 551. Irshad: vol. 2, p. 298. I'lam al-Wara: vol. 2, p. 109. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 121. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 50, pp. 116, 117. Manaqib Ibn Shahr Ashub: vol. 4, p. 382.
Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 99, p. 79. Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: p. 789.
Riyahin al-Shari'ah: vol. 3, p. 23. Manaqib Ibn Shahr Ashub: vol. 4, p. 433.
Manaqib Ibn Shahr Ashub: vol. 4, p. 432.
Manaqib Ibn Shahr Ashub: vol. 4, p. 432.

events.title: Eid al-Ghadir
events.text:
On this day in the tenth year of the Hijrah, the event of Ghadir took place on the return from the Farewell Pilgrimage, and during the three days that the caravan of one hundred and twenty thousand pilgrims halted at Ghadir Khumm, the Prophet (SAWW), in his longest sermon, introduced Ali ibn Abi Talib and the eleven Imams (PBUT) after him as the Imams of the people until the Day of Resurrection, and took allegiance from all that crowd.
The Great Eid of the Al-Muhammad (PBUT)
This day is counted as the greatest Eid of the Al-Muhammad (PBUT), because it is a momentous and great event coming after the toils of the prophets, successors and saints, and during it, by divine command, a public declaration was made of the immediate successorship of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (PBUH).
This day is a blessed heavenly Eid.
It is the day on which God Almighty saved Hazrat Ibrahim (PBUH) from the fire.
It is the day on which the repentance of Hazrat Adam (PBUH) was accepted.
It is the day on which God Almighty gave Hazrat Musa (PBUH) victory over the sorcerers.
It is the day on which Hazrat Musa (PBUH), in the presence of his community, made Joshua son of Nun his successor.
It is the day on which Hazrat Isa (PBUH) made Shim'un al-Safa' his successor.
The day on which Hazrat Sulayman (PBUH) took his subjects as witnesses to the succession of Asaf ibn Barkhiya.
It is the day of the pact of brotherhood the Prophet (SAWW) established among his companions.
On this day the Prophet would appoint his successors, and a visitation (ziyarah) of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) has been reported for this day.
sources: Tawdih al-Maqasid: p. 31. al-'Udad al-Qawiyyah: p. 166. Misbah al-Kaf'ami: vol. 2, p. 601. Manaqib Ibn Shahr Ashub: vol. 3, p. 37. Misbah al-Mutahajjid: p. 754. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 35, p. 150; vol. 95, p. 189. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 122.
