subsections.title: The Participants in the Ghadir Ceremony
subsections.text:
The story of Ghadir was as follows: on Saturday, four or five days before the end of Dhu al-Qa'dah of the year 10 AH, the Prophet (SAWW) performed the ritual bath and, together with 120 thousand Muslims, left Medina.
In this journey, the Exalted Lady Siddiqah Tahirah Fatimah Zahra (PBUH), Umm Hani the sister of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), Fatimah bint Hamzah, Umm Salamah and the other wives of the Prophet (SAWW), including Aisha and Hafsah, were present. Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) also entered Mecca from Yemen with a group of men.
sources: al-Kafi: vol. 4, p. 248. Tabaqat Ibn Sa'd: vol. 3, p. 235. Irshad al-Sari: vol. 6, p. 429.
Manaqib Ibn Shahr Ashub: vol. 3, p. 25. Tabaqat Ibn Sa'd: vol. 3, p. 235. Irshad al-Sari: vol. 6, p. 429.

subsections.title: The Divine Command for the Ghadir Ceremony
subsections.text:
After the performance of the Hajj rites, the divine command came that the knowledge and trusts of the prophets be handed over to Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) and that his wilayah be conveyed to the people.
The Prophet (SAWW) wept so much that his blessed beard became wet with tears. He asked God to protect him from the evil of the hypocrites. In Mina the Prophet (SAWW) delivered two sermons and made a general reference to the wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH). In Masjid al-Khayf, Gabriel descended and said that God says: convey the wilayah of Ali (PBUH) to the people, but he did not bring the promise of protection from the evil of the enemies. At Kura' al-Ghamim, Gabriel descended once more and brought this verse: Fala'allaka tarik ba'd ma yuha ilayka wa ta'iq bihi sadruka: “Perhaps you may leave out some of what is revealed to you and your breast be constrained by it.”
Once again the matter of wilayah was emphasized, but no verse came assuring his protection from the evil of the enemies.
The Prophet (SAWW) told Gabriel what the hypocrites were saying, and they set out.
At the beginning of the day of 18 Dhu al-Hijjah they reached Ghadir as well, and Gabriel descended again and brought verse 67 of Surah al-Ma'idah, which contained the conveying of the wilayah of the Master of Masters, Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), and his safety from the evil of the hypocrites: Ya ayyuha al-rasul balligh ma unzila ilayka min rabbika wa in lam taf'al fama ballaghta risalatahu wa Allahu ya'simuka min al-nas inna Allaha la yahdi al-qawm al-kafirin: “O Messenger, convey to the people what has been sent down to you from your Lord concerning Ali (PBUH), and if you do not do this, you have not conveyed the divine message, and God will protect you from the people. God does not guide the disbelieving people.”
sources: Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 37, p. 127.
Surah Hud: verse 12.

subsections.title: The Prophet (SAWW) on the Pulpit of Ghadir
subsections.text:
At noon, after the congregational prayer, the Prophet (SAWW) ascended a pulpit that stood beneath two ancient trees and had been built by Salman, Abu Dharr, Miqdad and Ammar, and he had Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) stand one step below him on the pulpit, while a number of hypocrites were in front of the pulpit.
After speaking about himself, about divine unity and the attributes of perfection of the Exalted Truth, and after stating a major portion of the lawful and unlawful rulings of God's religion, he spoke of the Arabs' past, their lives and beliefs, and the hardships he had endured. Then he said: There is an unbreakable bond between the Quran and the Ahl al-Bayt (PBUT), and they will not separate from one another until they come to me at the Pool of Kawthar on the Day of Resurrection.
Then he spoke of some of the virtues and merits of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), and emphasized several times the Imamate and wilayah of him and his descendants up to Hazrat Mahdi (PBUH). Then he said: It has been revealed to me: In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate, Ya ayyuha al-rasul balligh ma unzila ilayka min rabbika....
Then he said: O people, I have not fallen short in conveying what God sent down to me, and I shall explain the reason for the revelation of this verse. Gabriel descended upon me again and commanded me from God Almighty to announce at this place to every white and black person of every tribe that Ali ibn Abi Talib is the successor, deputy and Imam after me. After God and His Messenger, he is your guardian and master, and has more right over all of you than you yourselves. Concerning this, God has sent down a verse to me: Innama waliyyukum Allahu wa rasuluhu wa alladhina amanu alladhina yuqimun al-salata wa yu'tun al-zakata wa hum raki'un.
Then he said: I asked Gabriel to ask God to excuse me from conveying this matter, because I am aware of the fewness of the believers and the abundance of the hypocrites and those who mock Islam. Then he said: Ma'ashir al-nas, huwa al-imam al-mubin (“O people, he is the manifest Imam”), do not turn away from his wilayah. It is he who guides to the truth and acts by it. Give him precedence, for God has given him precedence, and accept him, for God has appointed him. O people, he is the Imam from God. The denier of his wilayah will not be forgiven and his repentance will not be accepted. After me, Ali is the best of all women and men. Accursed and subject to divine wrath is the one who rejects my word and does not agree with it.
Know that Gabriel has informed me that God Almighty says: Whoever shows enmity to Ali and does not love him, my curse and wrath be upon him.
Then he said: O God, be Thou witness. I have fulfilled my mission. I have conveyed what You commanded. I have made it clear to everyone. Be aware that, other than my brother Ali ibn Abi Talib (PBUH), no one else is Amir al-Mu'minin. The command of the believers after me is not lawful for anyone but Ali ibn Abi Talib (PBUH).
sources: Surah al-Ma'idah: verse 55.

subsections.title: The Introduction of Ali ibn Abi Talib (PBUH)
subsections.text: Here he took hold of Ali's (PBUH) arm, and at the same time Ali (PBUH) raised his blessed hands toward him. The Prophet (SAWW) lifted him up so high that Ali's blessed feet reached the Prophet's (SAWW) knees. Then he said: Alastu awla bikum min anfusikum? (“Am I not more entitled to you than yourselves?”) Everyone said: “O God, yes.” He said: Hadha Ali akhi wa wasiyyi, man kuntu mawlahu fa-hadha Ali mawlahu wa huwa Ali ibn Abi Talib. Whoever I am master and guardian of, he is the master of him. His place and rank are like my place and rank with you. O God, befriend whoever befriends him, and be an enemy to whoever is his enemy, and he spoke other words to emphasize the divine command and the people's acknowledgment. Then he said: Let those present convey the news of Ghadir to those absent, and fathers to their children, until the Day of Resurrection.

subsections.title: Pledge by Word and by Hand
subsections.text:
As soon as he came down from the pulpit, the people pledged allegiance in loud voices, with tongue and hand, and the Prophet (SAWW) was saying: Hanni'uni, hanni'uni, congratulate me.
Then he ordered that a separate tent be set up for Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), and said: Let everyone go and greet him and say: Peace be upon you, O Amir al-Mu'minin. Umar came and greeted him and said: Bakhin bakhin, ya Ibn Abi Talib, asbahta mawlaya wa mawla kulli mu'minin wa mu'minah (“Well done, well done, O son of Abu Talib, you have become my master and the master of every believing man and woman”).
Abu Bakr was also a partner with Umar in this congratulation. The pledge lasted three days, and during these three days they would pray the noon and afternoon prayers together. After the prayer the pledging continued until sunset, and they would also pray the evening and night prayers together.
sources: al-Ghadir: vol. 2, p. 276.
Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 38, p. 344. Mulhaqat al-Haqq: vol. 6, pp. 468, 469. al-Ghadir: vol. 1, which has reported this matter from 60 Sunni sources.
Fayd al-'Allam: p. 123, quoting al-Daraqutni and al-'Asimi.

subsections.title: The Women's Pledge
subsections.text:
For the women's pledge, they placed a vessel of water beneath a curtain, so that half of the vessel was on one side and the other half on the other side of the curtain. On one side Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) had placed his blessed hand in the vessel of water, and on the other side the women placed their hands and, while congratulating, said: “Peace be upon you, O Amir al-Mu'minin.”
The presence of Hazrat Siddiqah Tahirah (PBUH) adorned the ceremony.
On the other hand, Aisha's pledge recorded this precedent of hers in the minds, up to the day she started the Battle of Jamal, drew up ranks against the Master of Ghadir, and was defeated in humiliation and disgrace by the army of wilayah.
After the proclamation of wilayah at Ghadir, Gabriel descended and brought this verse: Al-yawm akmaltu lakum dinakum wa atmamtu 'alaykum ni'mati wa radiytu lakum al-Islama dina: “Today I have perfected your religion for you and completed My favor upon you and approved Islam as your religion.”
sources: Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 21, p. 38. 'Awalim: vol. 3/15, p. 309.
Surah al-Ma'idah: verse 3.

events.title: Killing of Uthman
events.text:
On this day in the year 34 AH, Uthman ibn Affan, after the Muslims besieged his house, at the age of 81 or 90, was killed by a man from the people of Egypt.
After killing him, they brought Uthman out of his house and threw him onto one of the garbage heaps of Medina. For fear of the Muhajirun and the Ansar, no one would bury him, until after three days, by stealth, they took him to the Jewish graveyard of Medina called “Hashsh Kawkab” and buried him. Mu'awiyah, during his caliphate, demolished the houses between this graveyard and Baqi' and joined it to the cemetery of the Muslims!
sources: Tarikh al-Khulafa': p. 162. Masar al-Shi'ah: pp. 21, 22. Tawdih al-Maqasid: p. 32. al-'Udad al-Qawiyyah: p. 166. Misbah al-Kaf'ami: vol. 2, p. 601. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 95, p. 189. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 125.
Masar al-Shi'ah: pp. 21, 22. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 125.

subsections.title: Uthman's Usurping Caliphate
subsections.text: Uthman took Umar ibn al-Khattab's place after him. During his lifetime Umar had said many times that after him the caliphate belonged to Uthman, but outwardly he left the matter of the caliphate to a council, and arranged it in such a way that it would end up with the caliphate of Uthman.
sources: Tarikh Dimashq: vol. 39, pp. 188, 189.

subsections.title: The Innovations of Uthman
subsections.text:
During the days he held power, Uthman committed major violations:
1) He built spacious and beautiful houses of stone, brick and plaster, with doors of Indian, fragrant and costly wood. He came to own many gardens, lands and springs, and amassed great wealth in his treasury. When he was killed, one hundred and fifty thousand dinars and one million dirhams were with his treasurer. This is in addition to the lands around Hunayn, worth one hundred thousand dinars, and the abundant cattle, sheep and camels that remained from him.
2) To a group such as Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf and Zubayr ibn al-Awwam he gave so much wealth, gardens and land that they too built houses of stone, brick and plaster. Zubayr alone left behind, after his death, fifty thousand dinars, a thousand slaves and a thousand horses.
3) He did not carry out retaliation against Ubayd Allah ibn Umar for the killing of three Muslims. After the burial of Umar ibn al-Khattab, Ubayd Allah, the son of Umar, since he could not get at Abu Lu'lu'ah, killed his young daughter at his door. He also killed Hurmuzan, a Persian Muslim, and Jufaynah, the slave of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, on the charge that a few days before Umar was killed he had seen those two talking with Firuz.
Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas threw Ubayd Allah ibn Umar to the ground, took his sword, and ordered his slaves to imprison him until the matter of the council was finished. When Uthman became caliph, Ali ibn Abi Talib (PBUH) and others said: “Carry out retaliation against him.” Uthman released him and said: Yesterday his father was killed, shall I kill his son today? As caliph of the Muslims, I have forgiven Ubayd Allah.
4) He brought Hakam ibn Abi al-As, the father of Marwan, who was an enemy of God and His Messenger, to Medina with honor. He was the uncle of Uthman, known for enmity toward the Prophet (SAWW) and the Ahl al-Bayt (PBUT). Because of the insolences he had committed against the Prophet (SAWW), Hakam had been exiled to Ta'if by the Prophet. After the martyrdom of the Prophet (SAWW), Abu Bakr and Umar did not accept Uthman's intercession for Hakam. As soon as power came into Uthman's hands, he brought his uncle Hakam and Marwan, with their entourage, to Medina, openly opposing the Prophet's (SAWW) command.
Not long after, in place of Hakam, he exiled Abu Dharr after much beating and abuse. On the other hand, he gave one hundred thousand dirhams of the Muslims' property to Hakam. He also gave the fifth of Ifriqiyah, which was one hundred thousand dinars and in which all the Muslims were partners, along with Fadak, to Marwan! He also chose Marwan as his minister and secretary of his secrets, whereas the Prophet (SAWW) had cursed Marwan and Hakam many times.
5) He made Walid ibn Uqbah, of whom the Prophet (SAWW) said: “He is of the people of the Fire,” governor of Kufa. Walid was a transgressor and a drinker of wine, and one night he drank wine with maidservants and singing girls until morning, and in the same state went to the mosque in the morning and prayed the dawn prayer with four rak'ahs and said: Would you like me to pray more! While prolonging his prostration he was saying: “Drink and give me to drink.”
sources: Muruj al-Dhahab: vol. 2, p. 341.
Muruj al-Dhahab: vol. 2, p. 341.
al-Ghadir: vol. 9, p. 260. Danistaniha-ye Tarikh: vol. 3, p. 223.
Shifa' al-Sudur fi Sharh Ziyarat al-'Ashura: vol. 1, p. 321.
Muruj al-Dhahab: vol. 2, pp. 343, 344.

subsections.title: The Killing of Uthman by the People
subsections.text:
In the end, a large number of the people of Kufa, Egypt and Basra came to Uthman in protest, and when he saw the situation was dangerous, using Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) as an intermediary, he promised to act on their demand, to replace the governors, and to adopt good conduct and justice. But as the protesters were returning to their cities, they saw Uthman's special courier traveling by a side road. They seized him and found a letter from Uthman written to the governor of Egypt: As soon as these people arrive, kill one, and cut off the hand of another.... They turned back, and many people joined them on the way to Medina, and they besieged his house for about fifty days.
During the days of the siege, Uthman asked Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) for water. The Imam brought three waterskins of cold water, but in the end the protesters poured into his house and an Egyptian man killed Uthman. Although Banu Hashim intervened, and according to one account Imam Hasan (PBUH) received a slight wound and Qanbar's head was wounded.
sources: Muruj al-Dhahab: vol. 2, p. 353.

events.title: The Outward Caliphate of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH)
events.text: On the day of Uthman's killing in the year 34 AH, the people pledged allegiance to Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH).
sources: Masar al-Shi'ah: pp. 21, 22. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 25. Tatimmat al-Muntaha: p. 16. Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 5, p. 212.

events.title: Departure of Ibrahim ibn Malik al-Ashtar to Fight Ibn Ziyad
events.text:
When Mukhtar (may God have mercy on him) had cleansed Kufa of the killers of the Master of the Martyrs (PBUH), on this day Ibrahim ibn Malik al-Ashtar, with 12,000 men, or according to Ibn Nama's narration with fewer than 20,000, left Kufa to fight Ibn Ziyad, and Mukhtar went out to see him off.
Ibrahim's army went as far as the bank of the Khazir river, five farsakhs from Mosul, and made that place its camp. Ubayd Allah came to Mosul and took it with thirty thousand or eighty thousand cavalry, and they prepared to fight Ibrahim's army.
On the night before the battle was to begin, sleep did not come to the eyes of Ibrahim ibn Malik, and he repeated these words many times to his army: “O people, you are the helpers of the religion and the Shia of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), and this is Ubayd Allah ibn Marjanah, the killer of Husayn ibn Ali (PBUH). This is the one who denied the son of Fatimah Zahra (PBUH) a sip of water while his women and children cried out ‘thirst.’ It was he who prevented the son of the Prophet (SAWW) from going anywhere, and they surrounded him until they martyred him with parched lips, and they mounted his women on camels like slave girls and took them to Sham. By God, the people of Pharaoh did not do to the Children of Israel what these accursed ones did to the descendants of the Prophet (SAWW).”
Then Ibrahim prayed that God grant us help and victory, since we have become wrathful to avenge the Ahl al-Bayt of the Prophet (SAWW).
In the morning he inspected the various parts of the army and the banners, and the battle began. In the end, after several days of fighting and the flight of the army of Ubayd Allah ibn Ziyad, on the day of Ashura of the year 67 AH, Ubayd Allah rushed to the depths of Hell at the hands of Ibrahim ibn Malik al-Ashtar al-Nakha'i, and his head was sent to Mukhtar.
sources: Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 45, pp. 380, 384. Fursan al-Hayja': vol. 2, pp. 235, 238.

events.title: Martyrdom of Maytham al-Tammar
events.text:
On this day in the year 60 AH, Maytham al-Tammar, because of his loyalty to Imam Husayn (PBUH), was hanged by Ibn Ziyad and was martyred.
The date of Maytham's martyrdom has also been reported as 19 Dhu al-Hijjah and as the day of Ashura.
sources: I'lam al-Wara: vol. 1, p. 343. Qala'id al-Nuhur: Dhu al-Hijjah vol., p. 416. Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: p. 131. Maraqid al-Ma'arif: vol. 2, p. 340. Waqa'i al-Shuhur: p. 240.
Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 5, p. 214.

events.title: Day of Mubahalah
events.text:
This day is, on the one hand, the day of the Mubahalah of the Ahl al-Bayt (PBUT) with the Christians of Najran, and on the other hand, the revelation of the verse of purification concerning the Ahl al-Bayt (PBUT) took place on this day.
When this verse was revealed, the Prophet (SAWW) summoned Ali, Fatimah, Hasan and Husayn (PBUT) and said: Allahumma ha'ula'i ahli: “O God, these are my family.”
The Prophet's (SAWW) Letter to the Christians of Najran
In the tenth year of the Hijrah, the Prophet (SAWW) sent a letter to the Christians of Najran, to the effect that they should worship the One God and become Muslims, or pay the jizyah to the Muslims and remain in their own religion, otherwise they should be prepared for war.
The people of Najran consulted in their great church; some, such as the Sayyid, who was one of the elders of the tribe, and the 'Aqib, who was the bishop of Najran, declared their opposition to submitting to the Prophet's (SAWW) demand. In contrast, some, such as Abu Harithah, the archbishop of Najran, who was 120 years old and secretly a Muslim, agreed with the Prophet's (SAWW) command. After two days of consultation, it was decided to read the book “al-Jami'ah,” which mentioned the attributes of the Prophet (SAWW) coming after Hazrat Isa (PBUH), and the scroll of Hazrat Seth (PBUH). In the presence of the Christians and the envoys of the Prophet (SAWW), the chapters of al-Jami'ah were read, and, acknowledging what was in al-Jami'ah, they decided to send seventy men, including the Sayyid, the 'Aqib and Abu Harithah, to Medina to investigate.
sources: Masar al-Shi'ah: pp. 22, 23. al-'Udad al-Qawiyyah: pp. 307, 308. Misbah al-Kaf'ami: vol. 2, p. 601. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 97, pp. 168, 384. Fayd al-'Allam: pp. 127, 129. Zad al-Ma'ad: p. 287.
Tarikh al-Khulafa': p. 169.

subsections.title: The Najranis in Medina
subsections.text:
They came to Medina and were received in the presence of the Prophet (SAWW). Whatever proof and argument he presented, they did not accept, and the order for Mubahalah was given. Gabriel (PBUH) descended and brought this verse: Faman hajjaka fihi min ba'di ma ja'aka min al-'ilmi faqul ta'alaw nad'u abna'ana wa abna'akum wa nisa'ana wa nisa'akum wa anfusana wa anfusakum thumma nabtahil fanaj'al la'nata Allahi 'ala al-kadhibin: “If anyone disputes with you about him after the knowledge that has come to you, say: come, let us summon our sons and your sons, our women and your women, and those who are as our own selves and your own selves; then let us invoke and call down God's curse upon the liars.”
So the Mubahalah was agreed upon, and the Sayyid and the 'Aqib went to their camp outside Medina. They consulted with one another, and some of their scholars said: “If tomorrow Muhammad comes to the Mubahalah with companions and a great crowd, this is the way of kings and do not let fear enter you. But if he brings the elect of his household, this is the work of prophets.”
sources: Surah Al Imran: verse 61.

subsections.title: The Mubahalah Ceremony
subsections.text:
The next day, at sunrise, the Prophet (SAWW) took the hand of Ali ibn Abi Talib (PBUH) and came out of his chamber. He sent Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn (PBUT) ahead, and Hazrat Siddiqah al-Kubra Fatimah Zahra (PBUH) came behind, until they reached the place between two trees that had been designated beforehand. Beforehand, by his order, the ground beneath those two trees had been swept, and a black cloak was placed over the trees as a canopy. The Muslims of Medina came as well, and the people of Najran came with their children. The Prophet (SAWW) sent someone to the Sayyid and the 'Aqib to say that we are ready.
The bishop came with his companions and said: With whom will you perform Mubahalah against us? The Prophet (SAWW) said: “With the best of the people of the earth and the finest of the worlds in the sight of God Almighty, for I have been commanded by God Almighty to bring them,” and he pointed to the Ahl al-Kisa' (PBUT).
As soon as the Sayyid, the 'Aqib and the bishop laid eyes on the Prophet (SAWW) and the Ahl al-Kisa' (PBUT), they were seized by terror, to the point that their faces turned yellow. Abu Harithah, who inclined toward Islam, seized the opportunity, stepped forward, took the hands of the Sayyid and the 'Aqib, pulled them back, advised them, and informed them of the consequences of this Mubahalah, and said: You have read his attributes and those of his household in the books. This Muhammad is that very Prophet; do you not see the black clouds, and the change in the sun, and the branches of the trees bent over, and the voice of the birds, and the black smoke around us and the signs of earthquake that have appeared in the mountains. Those honored ones are waiting to raise their hands in supplication. By God, if they speak a word, no trace of us will remain. Let us go and make peace with him.

subsections.title: The Najranis' Avoidance of Mubahalah
subsections.text:
They sent for him, and Abu Harithah became a Muslim and said: The people of Najran have become regretful. The Prophet said: Let them accept Islam. He said: They will not accept. He said: Let them be prepared for war. He said: They do not have the power for that, but they are ready to accept the jizyah.
The Prophet (SAWW) said to Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH): “Tell them the conditions of protection and its amount.” After he fixed the jizyah and its conditions, Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) brought them to the Prophet (SAWW), and the Prophet (SAWW) said: “If you had performed Mubahalah with me and this group of my household, you would have been turned into the form of monkeys and pigs, this valley would have become a blaze upon you, and a year would not have passed before all the Christians would have perished.”
sources: Tafsir al-Burhan: vol. 1, pp. 287, 288. Qala'id al-Nuhur: Dhu al-Hijjah vol., pp. 427, 438, 441.

events.title: Day of Ring-Giving
events.text:
On this day Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), in the Prophet's (SAWW) mosque, gave his ring to a beggar while in the state of bowing (ruku'), and the blessed verse Innama waliyyukum Allahu wa rasuluhu wa alladhina amanu alladhina yuqimun al-salata wa yu'tun al-zakata wa hum raki'un was revealed concerning him. Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) was asked about the meaning of this noble verse which says: Ya'rifun ni'mat Allah thumma yunkirunaha: “They recognize the blessing of God, then they deny it.” The Imam said: When the blessed verse Innama waliyyukum Allahu was revealed, a number of the companions of the Prophet (SAWW) gathered in the mosque of Medina. Some said to others: What do you say about this verse? Some said: If we deny this verse, we must deny the other verses too, and if we believe in this verse and accept it, it is humiliation for us, because Ali ibn Abi Talib (PBUH) will gain authority over us. A number of the hypocrites said: We know that Muhammad is truthful in what he says. We love him outwardly, but we will not obey Ali in what he commands.
The Imam said: At this time this verse was revealed: Ya'rifun ni'mat Allah thumma yunkirunaha,... meaning: they recognize the wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib (PBUH), while most of those who recognize it are disbelievers in his wilayah.
Some of the opponents have said: It has not happened for anyone to combine two acts of worship, one of wealth and one of the body, at one time, except Ali ibn Abi Talib (PBUH), and for no one have virtues come like those that have come for Ali (PBUH).
sources: Surah al-Ma'idah: verse 55.

Qala'id al-Nuhur: Dhu al-Hijjah vol., p. 426. The major Sunni authorities agree that the verse Innama waliyyukum Allah... was revealed concerning Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH). Among them are Fakhr al-Razi, Muhammad Sadr 'Alam, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Khatib al-Baghdadi, Ibn 'Asakir, Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Amir, Ibn al-Maghazili, Abu al-Layth al-Samarqandi, al-Tha'labi, Sibt Ibn al-Jawzi, Shihab al-Din Ahmad, Ibn al-Sabbagh, Abu Nu'aym, Mulla Ali Qushji, al-Sam'ani, al-Waqidi, al-Bayhaqi, al-Nasa'i, al-Khwarazmi, al-Tabari, al-Kalbi, al-Hamawayni and others.
Surah al-Nahl: verse 83.
Tafsir al-Burhan: vol. 1, p. 479.

events.title: Revelation of Surah Hal Ata
events.text:
On this day Surah “Hal Ata” was revealed concerning Amir al-Mu'minin, Fatimah Zahra, Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn (PBUT). This important event came after their three days of fasting and their giving of their iftar meals to the poor, the orphan and the captive, when heavenly food was sent down. According to one account, the blessed surah was revealed on 25 Dhu al-Hijjah.
Imam Sadiq (PBUH) said: That bowl in which food was brought from Paradise and which those honored ones ate from is with us, and Hazrat Sahib al-Amr (PBUH) will bring it out, and they will partake of heavenly food from it
sources: Zad al-Ma'ad: p. 301.
Tawdih al-Maqasid: p. 32. Masar al-Shi'ah: p. 23. Misbah al-Mutahajjid: p. 712. al-'Udad al-Qawiyyah: p. 315.
Zad al-Ma'ad: p. 301.

events.title: The First Friday Prayer of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH)
events.text: This day coincides with the first Friday on which Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), after the people's pledge of allegiance to him, performed the Friday prayer.
sources: Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: p. 159.

events.title: Death of Marwan
events.text:
On this day in the year 133 AH, Marwan ibn Muhammad ibn Marwan ibn al-Hakam, known as Marwan al-Himar, the last caliph of Banu Umayyah, was killed, and the thousand-month Umayyad dynasty came to an end.
After the uprising of the Abbasids under the leadership of Saffah, he sent his uncle Abd Allah ibn Ali to fight Marwan. Marwan had fled to Busir, in the region of Fayyum in Egypt, and along the way they killed every Umayyad they saw. On the bank of the Jordan river they killed a great number of people, spread a tablecloth over them, and ate. Abd Allah, the uncle of Saffah, said: “Whatever we do, it does not make up for the day of the martyrdom of Husayn ibn Ali (PBUH).” From there he sent a group with Umar ibn Isma'il to remove the threat of Marwan. At Busir they beheaded Marwan in a church and cut out his tongue, and a cat ate his tongue. Interestingly, the day before, Marwan had cut out the tongue of a slave, and that same cat had eaten it. Then they took his wife and children captive and sent them to Saffah. Some have reported this event on the 21st of this month.
sources: Tatimmat al-Muntaha: p. 146. Zad al-Ma'ad: p. 304. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 131.
Qala'id al-Nuhur: Dhu al-Hijjah vol., p. 413.

events.title: The Incident of Harrah
events.text:
On this day the Incident of Harrah took place, on a Wednesday in the year 63 AH, where the wording of the narration, “three days before the end of Dhu al-Hijjah,” gives the 27th or 28th.
It was on this day that, by order of the accursed Yazid, the killing and plundering of the people of Medina took place, and after killing more than 4,000 people, Musrif (Muslim) ibn Uqbah made the property and women of the people of Medina lawful for his army for three days. This event is known as the Incident of Harrah, and it occurred two and a half months before the death of the accursed Yazid.
sources: Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 18, pp. 125, 126. Qala'id al-Nuhur: Dhu al-Hijjah vol., p. 448. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 132.

events.title: Death of Ali ibn Ja'far (PBUH)
events.text:
On this day in the year 210 AH, Ali ibn Ja'far (PBUH) passed away. The imamzadah of lofty rank, Ali ibn Ja'far al-Sadiq (PBUH), was a noble sayyid, extremely pious, abounding in virtue, a scholar who acted upon his knowledge, and counted among the greatest reliable narrators. He lived in the time of Imam Sadiq, Hazrat Musa ibn Ja'far, Imam Reza and Hazrat Jawad (PBUT).
Ali ibn Ja'far (PBUH) was younger than his other brothers, and after the death of his honored father he always kept company with his brother Hazrat Musa ibn Ja'far (PBUH). He took the teachings of religion and many hadiths from him and narrated them, among them the book “Masa'il Ali ibn Ja'far.” Also attributed to him are “Masa'il al-Halal wa al-Haram” and “al-Manasik.”
sources: Qala'id al-Nuhur: Dhu al-Hijjah vol., p. 448. Subul al-Rashad ila Ashab al-Imam al-Jawad (PBUH): p. 175.
Subul al-Rashad ila Ashab al-Imam al-Jawad (PBUH): p. 175.

subsections.title: Ali ibn Ja'far's Reverence for the Station of the Imamate
subsections.text:
Muhammad ibn Hasan 'Ammar says: For 10 years in Medina the Radiant I was in the presence of Ali ibn Ja'far (PBUH), and I would listen to and write down the hadiths he had taken from his brother Hazrat Musa ibn Ja'far (PBUH).
One day I was with him when Hazrat Jawad (PBUH) entered the Prophet's (SAWW) mosque. As soon as Ali ibn Ja'far (PBUH) saw him, he rose from his place and hurried to him without shoes or cloak, kissed his hand, and honored and revered him. The Imam said: Uncle, sit, may God have mercy on you. Ali ibn Ja'far (PBUH) said: My master, how can I sit while you are standing.
When the Imam gave him permission, he returned to his place and sat in the gathering. His companions rebuked him: You are the uncle of his father! How do you treat him this way? Ali ibn Ja'far (PBUH) said: Be silent! Then he raised his hand, took hold of his beard, and said: The Exalted Truth did not make me worthy of the Imamate with this beard, but He made this young man worthy and entrusted the Imamate to him; given this, how can I deny his excellence and how can I not respect him, when I am his servant?
It is evident from this narration how great his knowledge was regarding the Imam of his time, and he is among the narrators whom all the scholars of rijal have praised eloquently.
sources: Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 47, p. 266. Subul al-Rashad ila Ashab al-Imam al-Jawad (PBUH): p. 179.

subsections.title: The Travels of Ali ibn Ja'far
subsections.text:
His residence was in the village of Urayd, four miles from Medina the Radiant, and for this reason he is called al-'Uraydi al-Madani, and his children are called the 'Uraydiyyun. His lineage continues from his four sons Muhammad, Ahmad, Hasan and Ja'far.
Ali ibn Ja'far (PBUH) was in Urayd or Medina when the people of Kufa asked him to honor Kufa with his residence. He accepted and for a time in Kufa devoted himself to spreading the teachings of religion and the hadiths of the Master of the Messengers and the guiding Imams (PBUT). After some time the people of Qom asked him to come to Qom. That honored one migrated from Kufa to Qom and remained in Qom until he joined divine sanctity, and he was buried outside Qom near the southern gate.
In two other places there are graves attributed to him: one in Urayd, one farsakh from Medina, and the other outside the city of Semnan.
Mas'udi gives the day of his death as 27 Dhu al-Hijjah, the year of his death as 233 AH, and his age as 72 years.
sources: Adapted from the books Anwar al-Mush'shi'in, Fasl al-Khitab, 'Umdat al-Talib, vol. 1, p., Tarikh-e Anjum-e Furuzan, Riyad al-Ansab, Rijal-e Kabirah, Rijal al-Kashshi, Muntaha al-Tawarikh.
Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: p. 226.
Muruj al-Dhahab: vol. 4, p. 127.

events.title: Death of Abu Bakr's Father
events.text: At the end of the year 13 AH, Abu Quhafah Uthman ibn Amir, the father of Abu Bakr, died at the age of 97, 99 or 104. Abu Quhafah accepted Islam on the day of the conquest of Mecca, and died in the time of Umar, six months and some days after the death of Abu Bakr.
sources: Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 5, p. 210. Sharh Ibn Abi al-Hadid: vol. 1, p. 156. Mustadrak al-Hakim: vol. 3, p. 244. al-Isti'ab of Ibn Abd al-Barr: vol. 8, p. 25. Muruj al-Dhahab of al-Mas'udi: vol. 2, p. 307.

events.title: Death of Hind the Liver-Eater
events.text:
In the year 13 AH, on the day of the death of Abu Quhafah, Hind the Liver-Eater, wife of Abu Sufyan and mother of Mu'awiyah, rushed to the depths of Hell. Hind was outwardly the wife of Abu Sufyan and the mother of Mu'awiyah, Utbah and Yazid, but she was among the women of the banner, to whom men would resort, and she had a great inclination toward black slaves, but whenever she gave birth to a black child, she would kill it. Mu'awiyah is attributed to four men: Musafir ibn Abi Amr, Umarah ibn al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, Abbas, and Sabbah, who was this accursed man, a singer of Umarah ibn al-Walid, a handsome youth who worked as a laborer for Abu Sufyan. Hind had a particular fondness for him, and for this reason the genealogists consider Utbah ibn Abi Sufyan to be from Sabbah as well.
When Hind became pregnant with Mu'awiyah, she did not wish to give birth to him at home. So she came to the side of Mount Ajyad and gave birth there, and it is for this reason that Hassan says:
لمن الصبی بجانب البطحاء فی التراب ملقی غیر ذی مهد
Whose is the child, cast on the ground at the side of the valley of Mecca, without a cradle?!!
sources: Tatimmat al-Muntaha: p. 43. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 18, p. 17.
Tatimmat al-Muntaha: p. 50. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 20, p. 549. Hamzah Sayyid al-Shuhada' (PBUH): pp. 26, 28. Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: p. 51.
Tatimmat al-Muntaha: pp. 46, 47.
Tatimmat al-Muntaha: p. 47.

subsections.title: The Bad Record of the Family of Mu'awiyah with Islam
subsections.text:
From this husband and wife and their son Mu'awiyah and grandson Yazid came harms and insolences toward the Prophet (SAWW), Amir al-Mu'minin, Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn (PBUT), which are mentioned in detail in the books of history and narrations.
Among them, on the route of the Quraysh disbelievers toward Uhud to fight the Prophet (SAWW), Hind intended to dig up the grave of his mother, Lady Aminah bint Wahb (PBUH), and commit an insolence, since Hind's father, mother and uncle had been killed at Badr. But the Quraysh disbelievers prevented her and said: “This will become a custom and they will do the same to our dead.” Hind said: Must I kill Muhammad, or Ali, or Hamzah? So she appointed Wahshi to this task and made promises to him. Wahshi said: “I am not able to kill the Prophet or Ali, but I will lie in ambush for Hamzah,” and with this preamble, on the command of the accursed Hind, he martyred that honored one.
On Hind's order, Wahshi split open the blessed chest of Hazrat Hamzah (PBUH), took out his liver, and bit into it like a dog, but the liver became like silver-colored stone and his teeth could not work on it, and he threw it on the ground, and from that day she was nicknamed “Akilat al-Akbad” (the Liver-Eater). Then she herself, with a dagger, cut off Hamzah's ears, nose and other parts, and hung them around her neck. With this crime she wounded the blessed heart of the Prophet (SAWW), and the Prophet, Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), Fatimah Zahra (PBUH), Safiyyah, the aunt of the Prophet (SAWW) and sister of Hamzah, and others wept. Despite all these crimes, the Prophet (SAWW) accepted the Islam of Hind and her husband, who had become Muslims under compulsion.
Ibn Abi al-Hadid says: Hind came to the Prophet (SAWW) with a number of Quraysh women, wearing a veil and covering herself because of the deeds she had committed against the Prophet (SAWW), especially the martyrdom of Hamzah (PBUH), and she feared that he would hold her to account.
The Prophet took a covenant and pledge from them that they would not associate partners with God Almighty, and stipulated other matters too, and they accepted. Hind spoke a word by which it was known that she was the wife of Abu Sufyan. The Prophet said: Are you Hind? She said: Yes, and outwardly she uttered the two testimonies of faith and asked for forgiveness. The Prophet (SAWW) said: You must no longer commit adultery. Hind said: Does a free woman commit adultery?! The Prophet (SAWW) said: And you must not kill children! Hind said: By my own life, I raised the children and you killed them at Badr.

events.title: The Prophet's (SAWW) Letters to the Great Kings
events.text: In this month in the year 6 AH, the Prophet (SAWW) wrote letters inviting the kings of various countries to Islam and monotheism, and sent them along with envoys.
sources: Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 20, p. 382.

events.title: Passing of Hazrat Abu Dharr
events.text:
In this month in the year 32 AH, Abu Dharr passed away in Rabadhah. He was the third, or fourth, or according to one account the fifth person to accept Islam, and then he returned to his tribe. Therefore he was not present at Badr, Uhud and Khandaq. After these three battles he came into the presence of the Prophet (SAWW) and was beside him until the Messenger of God (SAWW) was martyred.
The place and rank of Abu Dharr with the Messenger of God (SAWW) is greater than can be mentioned. The Prophet (SAWW) regarded Abu Dharr as the siddiq of the community and as resembling Isa ibn Maryam (PBUH) in asceticism. What is gathered from both Shia and Sunni reports is that after the rank of the infallibles (PBUT), among the companions no one has been like Salman al-Farsi, Abu Dharr al-Ghifari and Miqdad in majesty of station and loftiness of rank.
Imam Kazim (PBUH) says: On the Day of Resurrection a caller from the Lord of Might will call out: “Where are the disciples and the sincere of Muhammad ibn Abd Allah (SAWW), who stood firm on his path and did not break his covenant?” Salman, Abu Dharr and Miqdad will rise.
When Uthman usurped the caliphate, Abu Dharr was in Sham. He saw Mu'awiyah's worldliness and oppression and could not remain silent. So he opened his tongue in reproach and rebuke of Mu'awiyah, called the people to the wilayah of the rightful caliph of the Prophet (SAWW), Hazrat Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), and described his virtues to the people of Sham, in such a way that he made many of them incline toward Shi'ism.
Mu'awiyah reported Abu Dharr's condition to Uthman. Uthman wrote back to him to send Abu Dharr hurriedly to Medina on a fast mount with a harsh-tempered guide. Mu'awiyah sent Abu Dharr, a lean, tall old man, to Medina in the manner Uthman had instructed.
When Abu Dharr reached Medina, because of the severity of the road and the camel's lack of a saddle, his thighs were bloodied, and he entered upon Uthman with a bruised body, and Uthman was insolent to him and accused of lying the man whom the Messenger of God (SAWW) had called truthful.
In the end he ordered his exile to Rabadhah. He also said: Abu Dharr has no right to explain the rulings of religion to the people, and when he leaves Medina no one has the right to accompany him or speak with him.
When this news reached Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), he wept so much that his noble beard became wet with the tears of his blessed eyes, and he said: “Is this how they treat a companion of the Messenger of God (SAWW)? Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un!” Then the Imam, together with his two beloved ones, Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn (PBUT), and Aqil and Ammar Yasir, went to see Abu Dharr off, and each of them consoled Abu Dharr with words; although Marwan wanted to prevent it, Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) drove him away.
In this way Abu Dharr went with his family to Rabadhah, and there his son and his wife, who was a cousin of the Prophet (SAWW), died, and he informed his daughter of his own death, which the Messenger of God (SAWW) had told him on the return from Tabuk.
After Abu Dharr's passing, a caravan came from Iraq, and Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud prayed over him, and he was shrouded and buried by Malik al-Ashtar.
sources: al-Ghadir: vol. 8, p. 322. al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah: vol. 7, p. 185. Tatimmat al-Muntaha: p. 15.
Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: p. 32. Muntaha al-Amal: vol. 1, pp. 117, 118. Abu Dharr al-Ghifari: pp. 30, 40. Maraqid al-Ma'arif: vol. 1, pp. 101, 102.

events.title: Death of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari
events.text:
In the month of Dhu al-Hijjah of the year 44 AH (and according to one account the year 42 or 52), Abd Allah ibn Qays, known as Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, went to his doom. After the Hijrah, in the last years of the life of the Messenger of God (SAWW), he outwardly accepted Islam, and he was so well known for hypocrisy and for being in accord with Umar that he has been counted among the party of Umar.
Abu Musa, on the Night of the Bed (Laylat al-Mabit) on the night of the Hijrah, on the Night of Aqabah during the Battle of Tabuk, and also on the return from Ghadir at the pass of Harshi, was among those who intended to kill the Prophet (SAWW) and made the attempt, but God protected His Prophet.
He was the first to address Umar as “Amir al-Mu'minin.” Because of the trust Umar had in Abu Musa, he made him governor of Basra for four years, even though he did not keep anyone in a post for more than one year. Abu Bakr gave him no responsibility and Uthman dismissed him from the governorship of Basra.
At the Battle of Jamal he prevented the people from going to aid Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), until Imam Hasan (PBUH) came and called the people to aid the Imam, and the people responded.
Finally, in the affair of the two arbitrators at Dumat al-Jandal, he colluded with Amr ibn al-As and deposed Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) from the caliphate. After that, out of fear of the companions of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), he fled to Mecca and went to his doom there.
sources: Tarikh Dimashq: vol. 32, p. 100. Tadhkirat al-Huffaz: vol. 1, p. 24. Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: pp. 63, 214. Ightiyal al-Nabi (SAWW): pp. 72, 78. Tatimmat al-Muntaha: p. 41. Sharh Nahj al-Balaghah of Ibn Abi al-Hadid: vol. 31, pp. 303, 305. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 28, p. 99.

events.title: Death of Zurarah
events.text:
In this month in the year 148 AH, two months after the martyrdom of our master and lord Hazrat Sadiq (PBUH), Zurarah ibn A'yan passed away. On the day of the martyrdom of Imam Sadiq (PBUH) he was on his sickbed. Some have given the death of Zurarah as the year 150 AH.
He was among the companions of Imam Baqir, Imam Sadiq and Imam Kazim (PBUT), and held a special standing and rank with those honored ones.
He was a jurist, theologian, poet and man of letters, and it is well known that he was among the first jurists of the companions of the Imams (PBUT). His name was Abd Rabbih, his title was Zurarah, and his kunyah was Abu al-Hasan, and he is sometimes also called Abu Ali. His father was named A'yan ibn Sunsun. The children of Zurarah are Hasan, Husayn, Rumi, Ubayd, Abd Allah and Yahya.
He was a handsome and sturdy man, upon whose forehead the marks of worship were apparent, and he had a special, fine dignity. People would gather to see him and wait, and at times the crowd was such that Zurarah would return home.
Ibn Abi Umayr, who is one of the great figures of the Shia, says: When I was benefiting from the company of Jamil ibn Darraj (may God have mercy on him), I said to him: “How fine is your company and how adorned is the benefit from your gathering!” Jamil said: “But by God, we are before Zurarah like schoolchildren before their teacher.”
sources: Musnad Zurarah ibn A'yan: pp. 23, 24.
Ikhtiyar Ma'rifat al-Rijal (Rijal al-Kashshi): pp. 133-142.
Musnad Zurarah: p. 26.
Musnad Zurarah ibn A'yan: p. 29. Muntaha al-Amal: vol. 2, p. 171.
